deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page studies the algebraic equation x^7 + 28x^4 - (280 + 200 cos φ) = 0, headed 'kritische Punkte'. Its root x is a multivalued function of φ. Gauss finds the values of φ at which two roots coincide (the branch points). For each, he solves cos φ = given number for complex φ = f + ig, then evaluates the result numerically with logarithms. The next page is an envelope addressed to Gauss from Hannover, 23 Feb., so the problem probably arrived in a letter.

(1) CRITICAL POINTS.
- Let F(x) = x^7 + 28x^4. A double root needs F'(x) = 7x^6 + 112x^3 = 0, so x = 0 or x^3 = -16. Gauss writes -∛16.
- At x^3 = -16 we have x^6 = 256. Then x^7 + 28x^4 = x(x^6 + 28x^3) = x(256 - 448) = -192x.
- For the real root x = -∛16 this gives 192·∛16 = 16^{7/3}·(-1)·(-1)... more simply: x^7 = -2^{28/3} = -16·2^{16/3} and 28x^4 = 28·2^{16/3}. Hence F = 12·2^{16/3}, which Gauss writes '12.2^{16/3}'.
- The condition 280 + 200 cos φ = 12·2^{16/3} gives cos φ = 0.06·2^{16/3} - 1.4 = +1.0190484. The line '0,06.2^{16/3}' is the term 12/200·2^{16/3}.
- The complex roots x = ∛16·e^{±iπ/3} give F = -96∛16 ∓ 96√3∛16·i. Hence cos φ = -2.6095242 ∓ 2.0949574i.
- For the imaginary part Gauss uses √3·∛16/2 = ⁶√108. So the imaginary part is (192/200)·⁶√108.
- On the left half he computes log 192 = 2.2833012 and (1/6)·log 108 = 0.3389040. Their sum, 2.6222052, minus log 200 gives log of 2.0949574.
- The struck value '1,6222052 i' is the slip of writing the logarithm's digits instead of the number. It was then corrected to 2,0949574 i.
- The root x = 0 gives cos φ = -280/200 = -1.4.

(2) INVERTING cos(f + ig) = p ± iq.
- Gauss writes cos(f+ig) = cos f·cosh g - i·sin f·sinh g, in his notation cos f/cos h - i·sin f·tg h. Here cos ig = cosh g = 1/cos h and sinh g = tan h, so h is the Gudermannian of g.
- He puts p = cos f/cos h and q = sin f·tan h. With these definitions cos(f+ig) = p - iq.
- Eliminating h: 1/cos h = √(1 + q²/sin²f). Hence p² = cos²f + q²cos²f/sin²f.
- With c = cos²f this becomes the quadratic c² - (1+p²+q²)c + p² = 0. This is the top-right 'pp - (1+pp+qq)cos f² + cos f^4' [the vanishing is my reading].
- So 2cos²f = 1+p²+q² ± √((1+p²+q²)² - 4p²). The right half omits the factor 2; the left half has it as '2cos f² = 1+rr ± √{(1+rr)² - ...}'.
- The discriminant is expanded as 1 - 2p² + 2q² + (p²+q²)² (unfinished on the page).
- Bottom right, with t = tan f: p² = 1/(1+t²) + q²/t², so p²(t² + t⁴) = t² + q² + q²t².

(3) LEFT HALF: MODULUS-ARGUMENT SOLUTION.
- Gauss sets 1+p = a cos t, q = a sin t and 1-p = b cos β, q = b sin β. So a = |1+p+iq| and b = |1-p+iq|.
- The discriminant factors: (1+p²+q²)² - 4p² = a²b². Also a² + b² = 2(1+p²+q²).
- Hence 2cos²f = (a² + b²)/2 - ab, i.e. cos f = (a-b)/2. Correspondingly cosh g = cos ig = (a+b)/2. Gauss writes '(a+b)/2 = cos ig, (a-b)/2 = cos f'. The sign of cos f comes out right automatically, because a² - b² = 4p.
- He also uses half-angles: cos½(f±ig) = √((1+p ∓ iq)/2) = √(a/2)·e^{∓it/2}, and sin½(f±ig) = √((1-p ± iq)/2).
- From the addition theorems he gets sin f = √(ab)·cos½(A+B) and sin(ig) = i·√(ab)·sin½(A+B), with A = t and B = β.
- The struck 'r cos ψ + i r sin ψ' and the 'rr' expressions are an abandoned polar parametrisation.

(4) NUMERICS.
- cos φ = 1.0190484: φ = 0 + ig with log10(cosh g + sinh g) = 0.0846291.
- Divide by M = 0.4342945 (log M = 9.6377843) and multiply by 206265 (log = 5.3144251). Then log g'' = 8.92752 + 5.6766408 = 4.60416, so g = 40194'' = 11°9'54''. Hence φ = 0 + 11°9'54''·i.
- For z = -2.6095242 ± 2.0949574i: a = 2.641858, b = 4.173430. Then cos f = -0.765786, giving f = 139°58'37'' (Gauss: 139°58'38.88'').
- Also cosh g = 3.40764, so g = 1.89692 rad and log10 e^g = 0.82382. That is 2 × 0.41186.
- The column 0.41186 → 9.61475 → +5.67664 → 195609'' = 54°20'9'' equals ½g. So 54°20'9'' belongs to the half-angle computation of the complex branch point.
- The entries 106°1'45'' and 0.8033173 do not match this g or any obvious companion quantity. They are likely an abandoned trial.
- The row '180° + 54°20'9''i' seems mislabelled or belongs to a half-angle; for cos φ = -1.4 one should have φ = 180° + i·0.86701 rad (49°40'33'').
errors: Right half: 'cos f² = (1+pp+qq) ± √((1+pp+qq)² - 4pp)' lacks the factor 2 on the left. It should be 2cos²f; the left half has it correctly.
p = -cos f·√(1+qq/sin²f): with p = cos f/cos h as defined, the sign should be + (or ±, depending on the sign of cos h). The minus is a slip or a branch choice.

With p = cos f/cos h and q = sin f·tg h, cos(f+ig) equals p - iq, not p + iq. The left half (√((1+p)/2 - iq/2) = cos½(f+ig)) is consistent with this; the next page's 'p+iq = cos(f+ig)' has the opposite sign.
Imaginary part first written as 1.6222052 i: this is the logarithm's digits (log of 192·⁶√108 = 2.6222052) copied by mistake. Gauss struck it and corrected it to 2.0949574 i.

Numbers 106°1'45'' and 0.8033173 are inconsistent with the correct g = 1.89692 rad (log10 e^g = 0.82382) for cos φ = -2.6095242 ± 2.0949574i. They are also inconsistent with each other (0.8033173 corresponds to 105°58'50''), suggesting an abandoned or erroneous trial.

The row '180° + 54°20'9'' i' with 0.41186 does not give cos φ = -1.4: cosh(0.94834) = 1.484. The value 54°20'9'' is exactly half of g for the complex branch point, so the row label/association is doubtful.

results.what: Branch (critical) values of φ for x^7 + 28x^4 = 280 + 200cos φ, from F'(x) = 0. They are cos φ = 1.0190484, -2.6095242 ± 2.0949574i and -1.4, with φ = 11°9'54''·i for the first.
results.modern_name: Branch points / discriminant locus of an algebraic function (critical values of a polynomial map)
results.usually_credited_to: Puiseux (1850), Riemann (1851/1857) for the systematic theory; the computation itself is elementary

results.what: Inversion of cos(f+ig) = p - iq for real f, g, via a quadratic for cos²f with discriminant factoring as |1+z|²|1-z|²
results.modern_name: Complex arccosine via real quadratic: cos²f = [(1+|z|²) - √((1+|z|²)² - 4p²)]/2

results.what: cos f = (|1+z| - |1-z|)/2 and cosh g = (|1+z| + |1-z|)/2, with sin f = √(ab)·cos½(A+B) and sinh g = √(ab)·sin½(A+B) from half-angle square roots
results.modern_name: Elliptic-coordinate formula for arccos of a complex number (focal-distance form, cf. A&S 4.4.37; Kahan-style)
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in elliptic coordinates (Lamé, 19th c.); explicit tabulated form in later handbooks

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful but routine. It computes the critical values of a trinomial-type algebraic equation and inverts the cosine for complex arguments using elegant but classical identities: the elliptic-coordinate focal-distance formula and half-angle products. Gauss's fluency with complex trigonometry is well known. The mildly notable point is that he locates branch points of x(φ) in the complex φ-plane, a Riemann-surface-style concern, but nothing here anticipates a major later result.

checkable.asserts: cos φ at the real critical point x = -∛16 equals 1.0190484
Complex critical value cos φ = -2.6095242 - 2.0949574i (conjugate for e^{-iπ/3})
The discriminant factors as a²b² (should be 0)
cos f = (a-b)/2 for cos(f+ig) = p - iq (should be ~0)
f ≈ 139.977° (139°58'37'') and g ≈ 1.89692 rad for the complex branch point
p²(t²+t⁴) = t² + q² + q²t² when p² = 1/(1+t²) + q²/t² (should be 0)
cos(f+ig) = cos f cosh g - i sin f sinh g (should be 0)
For cos φ = -1.4, g = 0.86701 rad (not 0.94834), showing the '180°+54°20'9''i' label is not this root

transcription_corrections: The top-right expression is pp - (1+pp+qq)cos f² + cos f^4 (= 0); the '4/?' and '+4cos f^4' readings are doubtful.
Left half 'cos f^2' line begins '2cos f² = 1+rr ± √{(1+rr)² - ...}'; the leading mark is the factor 2.
'2r sin β' line likely reads (1-rr)² + (2r sin β)² (part of the discriminant in polar form).
'cos½A + B' and '√b(cos B - i sin B)' use A = t, B = β; the final formulas read √ab·cos½(A+B) = sin f and i√ab·sin½(A+B) = sin ig.
'√((1+p)/2 - iq/2) = cos½(f+ig) √2 cos½t + i sin½t...' is a separate side note √(a/2)(cos½t - i sin½t), not a factor of the equation.
